references.text: John the Baptist himself confesses that he is not the Christ – he is not the light, but points to the light. See [ref:Joh 1:20|John 1:20].
John was sent from God to testify about the light, so that all might believe through him. Verse 8 clarifies that he himself was not the light, but only a witness. See [ref:Joh 1:6-7|John 1:6-7].
The true light that gives light to everyone was coming into the world – in contrast to John, who only testified about this light. See [ref:Joh 1:9|John 1:9].
John the Baptist says himself: "I am not the Messiah, but I have been sent ahead of him." He emphasizes that he must decrease while Christ must increase. See [ref:Joh 3:28-30|John 3:28-30].
Jesus refers to John as a lamp (λύχνος) that burned and shone, but distinguishes between the lamp and the true light (φῶς). See [ref:Joh 5:35|John 5:35].
Jesus declares "I am the light of the world" – he is the true light that John was not, but about which John testified. See [ref:Joh 8:12|John 8:12].

Paul explains that John's baptism was a baptism of repentance, and that John himself told the people to believe in the one who would come after him, namely Jesus. John also pointed forward to the light. See [ref:Apg 19:4|Acts 19:4].
John the Baptist testifies that the one coming after him is stronger than he – he is only a forerunner and a witness, not the light itself. See [ref:Matt 3:11|Matthew 3:11].
